correctness.rationale: Every nontrivial block is independently transitive. The five directed-edge orbit types are classified, with forbidden types eliminated by indegree or cycle obstruction. Compatible orbits form precisely a join of a complete directed-forest complex and one discrete parent-choice complex per block. Orbit barycenters triangulate the actual geometric fixed space. The classical complete-digraph forest theorem and join homology prove the sphere multiplicities over integers. A standalone finite oracle verified 490 orbits and 142870 orbit-subset comparisons across 46 cases; experiments are only corroboration.

originality.rationale: Primary sections of the 2026 strong Morse simplex paper give ordinary homotopy and the rooted-forest skeleton, not geometric block-product fixed loci. An earlier full open-access directed-tree text establishes underlying definitions and shellability without the stated fixed-locus classification. The closest published character formulas concern equivariant Euler traces or a different isolated forest model, so neither gives the asserted PL join and all-degree integral homotopy type. Statement-implication comparisons of several targeted searches found no covering theorem. A full 1999 publisher paper and unindexed literature remain uncertainties.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of actual fixed point spaces for a broad infinite family of independent block-transitive group actions. The uniformity in block sizes and group choices, the empty/contractible/spherical phase distinctions, exact PL join model and unbounded sphere dimensions are structural features unavailable from ordinary homotopy data. It is not a specialized table recomputation or mere normalizing substitution.
